clue.text: Set found in San Francisco, Horta and elsewhere

indicators.note: something found in a place is sitting inside it, so look inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one place name and the start of the next
surface padding that rounds off the list of places

explanation.surface: A group of people turning up in San Francisco, in Horta in the Azores, and in other places.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the tail of Francisco into Horta; 'and elsewhere' only finishes the travelogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A cohort is a group of people sharing a feature, which a set also is.

clue.text: Potter about to make them?

blocks.note: surface reading: to potter about is to pass the time idly doing small jobs
setter's reading: a potter, the craftsman, is about to make some pots and dishes

explanation.walkthrough: The verb 'potter about' hides the noun potter, someone who makes fired clay ware, followed by 'about to', meaning on the point of.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceramics are the fired clay pots and dishes that a potter produces at the wheel and kiln.

clue.text: Oh, no! Lulu's on the rampage somewhere in the Pacific

indicators.note: something on the rampage runs wild, so these letters are thrown out of their order

blocks.note: the exclamation and the singer's name, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Alarm as the singer Lulu goes wild at a Pacific location.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Lulu's stands for 'is', joining the fodder to its indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Honolulu is the capital of Hawaii, an island state in the middle of the Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Player initially in the attack is fast

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it
in places the first piece inside the word that follows it

blocks.note: the first half of a raid, an attack
first letter of player
the rest of the raid, closing round the inserted letter

explanation.surface: A sports report: the player leading the attack is quick.
explanation.walkthrough: A RAID is an attack; the player's first letter goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid and fast are synonyms, both meaning moving at great speed.

clue.text: Bird painter?

blocks.note: first meaning: a family of songbirds of Australasia
second meaning: James McNeill ..., the American artist famed for the portrait of his mother

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it seems to ask for an artist who paints birds; the two words are separate meanings of one name.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to an Australasian songbird and to a celebrated nineteenth-century American artist.

clue.text: When he does, a spinner can be difficult to play, paradoxically

definitions.text: When he does, a spinner can be difficult to play, paradoxically

blocks.clueFragment: When he does, a spinner can be difficult to play
blocks.note: setter's reading: a spin bowler's ball landing on a rough spot of the pitch turns unpredictably and is hard for the batsman
surface reading: the phrase usually means going through a spell of poor form, the opposite of a bowler doing well

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a spinner is a slow bowler who makes the ball turn off the pitch; worn patches make it turn sharply. The idiom normally means a run of bad luck, hence 'paradoxically'.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally, the idiom for suffering a poor spell describes a bowler's ball striking a worn part of the pitch.

clue.text: Have a break from Arran and rest somewhere else in Scotland

indicators.note: to break something is to smash it apart, so the words from it are broken and rebuilt

blocks.note: the Scottish island, taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A holiday tip: take a break from the island of Arran and relax in another Scottish spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde, which explains 'else' in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranraer is a port town in Galloway in south-west Scotland, so it is another place in that country.

clue.text: Learners in the ring proceed in an ungainly way

indicators.note: in the means set inside what follows, so the first piece sits within the second

blocks.note: the opening of a loop, a ring
L is the learner-driver plate, doubled for the plural
the rest of the loop

explanation.surface: Beginners in a boxing or circus ring move clumsily.
explanation.walkthrough: Two Ls go inside LOOP, a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: To lollop is to move with an awkward bounding gait, like a big dog or a hare.

clue.text: Versifier plays with myrrh around the orient

indicators.note: someone who plays with something fiddles it around, so these letters get moved about
around says the rearranged letters surround the next piece

blocks.note: the first four letters once the gift of the Magi is jumbled
the orient is the east, abbreviated E
the remaining letter of the jumble

explanation.surface: A poet experiments with the perfume of myrrh, an eastern resin.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhymer is someone who writes verse, often weak verse, which is what a versifier is.

clue.text: Hastily make cry of encouragement to batsman!

blocks.note: first meaning: to ... a dress or curtains is to sew them quickly
second meaning: urging a cricket batsman forward to score runs

explanation.walkthrough: A batsman is a batter in cricket, who scores by running between the wickets.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to sew something together quickly, and taken literally it urges a batsman to dash for runs.

clue.text: Later mutated into a flower? Exactly!

indicators.note: something mutated has changed its form, so these letters change their order
into puts the changed letters inside the word that follows

blocks.note: the first half of lily, a flower
the word later with its letters rearranged
the end of the lily

explanation.surface: A plant enthusiast exclaims that something later turned into a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exactly!' looks like a reply to the question but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally means in the strict, precise sense of the words, so it can stand for exactly.

clue.text: Spring at night? The consequences of it are unknown!

definitions.text: The consequences of it are unknown
definitions.note: a description of the answer rather than a synonym

blocks.note: a spring is a jump
at night one is in darkness

explanation.surface: A question about jumping at night, then a warning that nobody knows where it ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds the literal picture of jumping blind; the second sentence describes the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: A leap in the dark is an idiom for a risky act whose outcome cannot be foreseen.

clue.text: Tune mainly hit a sensational performance

indicators.note: mainly means most but not all, so the last letter of the word before is dropped

blocks.note: a tune is a melody
to ram is to hit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A catchy tune largely made a hit of a dramatic show.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is a play full of exaggerated, sensational incidents and emotions.

clue.text: So upset with one — keep your head out of it!

definitions.text: keep your head out of it
definitions.note: a jokey description of the answer rather than a synonym

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over, so these letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to someone so distressed that they should stay out of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep your head out of it' sounds like advice to avoid getting involved, but literally warns against the hangman's loop.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is the looped rope of a gallows, which you would want your head kept clear of.

clue.text: Stopped the action — 24 hours named after it

indicators.note: after says the piece before it is placed following the two pieces that come next

blocks.note: named means called
taken as written
twenty-four hours is a day

explanation.surface: A director halts filming, with a day's work named after the event.
explanation.definitionFit: To call it a day is an idiom for stopping work, which is ending the action.

clue.text: Detail from menu eater ordered

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new sequence, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A restaurant scene: a diner picks out a detail from the menu and orders it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads as a diner ordering food; here it signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To enumerate is to list items one by one, which is to detail them.

clue.text: County run out after heavy rain

indicators.note: after says the piece just before it comes second, behind the first word

blocks.note: County Down is in Northern Ireland
to pour is to run out, as liquid from a jug

explanation.surface: A cricket county side are run out after a heavy shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run out' suggests a cricket dismissal but means flow.
explanation.definitionFit: A downpour is a sudden heavy fall of rain.

clue.text: Offer half duly in a caring manner

indicators.note: half means only two of the four letters of the following word survive

blocks.note: to tender is to offer
taken as written, before half is removed

explanation.surface: A proposal made only half as properly as it should be, but kindly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderly means gently and with affection, which is how a caring person acts.

clue.text: Appropriate word produced for several functions?

definitions.text: Appropriate word produced for several functions?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone has come up with just the right term for something
setter's reading: the right term for an item that has many uses

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like praise for apt vocabulary; it is a description of the adjective you would apply to a many-use gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with several uses or functions is described with this adjective, built from 'many' and 'aims'.

clue.text: Mrs Beckham for Queen? No, more upmarket!

blocks.note: Victoria Beckham was Posh Spice in the Spice Girls
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone proposes Victoria Beckham as Queen, and is told she is too grand already.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria Beckham, a former Spice Girl, was nicknamed Posh Spice; 'for Queen' sets the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Posher is the comparative of posh, meaning more smart and upper-class, as upmarket goods are.

clue.text: Live exchange in policeman''s description of part of trunk

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: the answer describes a part of the torso

indicators.note: an exchange swaps things around, so these letters change places
in puts the rearranged letters inside the word that follows

blocks.note: PC, police constable, is a policeman; this is its first letter
the word live rearranged
the rest of PC

explanation.surface: A live broadcast of a constable describing part of a tree trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' suggests a tree or elephant; it means the human torso.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelvic is the adjective for the pelvis, the bony basin at the base of the human torso.

clue.text: Orders English stout

blocks.note: an OBE is an Order of the British Empire honour; plural here
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone asks for English stout, the dark beer, at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' looks like the beer being ordered but is the adjective meaning fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means very overweight, and stout is a polite word for a heavily built person.

clue.text: Instated in state?

blocks.note: surface reading: placed in an office or position
setter's reading: placed with full ceremony and grandeur on a throne

explanation.walkthrough: 'In state' means with official pomp, and also echoes the word instated itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is ceremonially installed on the throne at a coronation, which is being instated with pomp.

clue.text: Girl who first had cider?

blocks.note: surface reading: a young woman tasting cider for the first time
setter's reading: in the title of Laurie Lee's memoir the drink comes first, then with this girl

explanation.walkthrough: Laurie Lee's 1959 memoir of a Cotswold childhood is 'Cider with ___', in which the narrator first drinks cider with this girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The girl's name follows cider in the famous book title and she shares the narrator's first taste of it.

clue.text: Just try to host a party

blocks.note: first meaning: to have a go at something
second meaning: a bash is a party, so to have one is to throw a party

explanation.walkthrough: 'Have a bash' is informal British for have a go, and a bash is also slang for a lively party.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means attempting something, and literally means throwing a party since bash is slang for one.

clue.text: River trips ending at the beginning

indicators.note: the last letter is lifted round to the front of the word

blocks.note: tours are trips

explanation.surface: Boat trips on a river that finish where they started.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stour is the name of several English rivers, in Kent, Dorset and East Anglia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stour is a river, the name shared by several waterways in southern and eastern England.

clue.text: Repeatedly verifies (with reference to money orders, say)

blocks.note: re means concerning or with reference to
the US spelling of cheques, written orders to pay money; 'say' marks an example

explanation.surface: Someone double-checks things, especially their cheques.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheques are written CHECKS in American spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To recheck is to verify again, so rechecks means verifies once more.

clue.text: New? Before time, almost

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
early means before the expected time

explanation.surface: Is it new? It came ahead of schedule, more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly and almost are synonyms, both meaning not quite.
